paragraphs.text: Yargle is a gluttonous Frog Spirit that haunts the great Dominarian swamp of Urborg .
Yargle is a 50-foot-tall swamp spirit that was once a frog. He has a terrifyingly large mouth, empty eye sockets, wicked claws, and a half dozen small, skittering legs.
Belzenlok 's lieutenant Yar-Kul became too ambitious and was transformed into a maggot by the demon lord. That maggot was eaten by a frog, which later grew into Yargle.
Yargle was the first defense of the Stronghold when the Skyship Weatherlight attacked the Cabal . He was in turn dragged back into the swamp by Muldrotha .

When the demonic frog spirit Yargle first noticed the Phyrexians charging toward him, he was elated: so much food, all so eager to be eaten! What he didn't realize was that the more he ate, the more he exposed himself to the dangerously virulent glistening oil. Someone else noticed, though: Muldrotha , an Urborg elemental who was the daughter of the maro-sorcerer Multani . Seeing the danger that Yargle was in, she sent a plea for assistance to her father. Muldrotha managed to persuade him, and Multani bound himself to Yargle, using his powers and existing knowledge of Phyrexia to grant increased resistance to glistening oil. Though Multani had been initially reluctant to help, he found himself impressed by the insatiable nature of Yargle's appetite and gained a new appreciation for Urborg's strange ways.
After the invasion, Multani and Muldrotha gained a grudging respect for the bizarre monster, which he seemed to reciprocate by not trying to eat them.

In the Echoverse , Yar-Kul was a wandering chef with the most refined palate in all of Otaria . But when he entered Krosa , he mutated into a strange beast now feared by the populace. Retaining his discerning preferences, he used his many powerful legs to stomp any dish that didn't appeal to his tastes flat, along with the trespasser that brought it to him. However, his intervention in the Second Brothers' War, where he attacked the forces of the Cabal as they invaded, earned him some appreciation with the locals. As thanks, they began a yearly tradition of sending nine chefs into Krosa to present him with their finest meals.
